Its speed and trajectory make italmost unstoppable by the air defense systems available to Ukraine. It is only the third time Russia has used the missile. -@CNN

I’ve been asking European officials and diplomats for their reaction to U.S. force reductions and other attacks on the alliance for months and not one has told me this is “business as usual.”


Teri Schultz (@terischultz)

#NATO chief Rutte calls the expected US reduction in its contributions to the NATO Force Model (alliance's response to crises), to be discussed among deputy political directors Friday at NATO HQ, have been underway for a year. He calls them "structured" and "business as usual.

Leaders ignore this analysis at their own peril:


Giorgi Revishvili (@revishvilig)

General Zaluzhnyi, former Commander-in-Chief of Ukraine’s Armed Forces current Ambassador to the UK:

International order is in a stage of disintegration. 

International alliances, above all NATO, have lost part of their ability to guarantee the security of their members. 1/15

Breaking: The Trump administration’s push for a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund has derailed the Senate GOP plans to pass a major immigration enforcement package, with senators leaving Washington for their Memorial Day recess.

Republican senators said they were blindsided by the Justice Department’s fund, which was announced just this week, and are now at odds over how to rein it in.

As Russia accuses Ukraine of launching drones from Latvian territory, Latvia’s FM @Braze_Baiba tells me the “real reason” is that the Kremlin “needs to blame someone else for the fact that Russia can’t defend itself against long-range Ukrainian precision strikes.”

Video

Question: The NYT is reporting the regime change plan for Iran included reinstalling Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as leader.
Was that wise or practical?

Rep @jahimes: “Let me use the right word, which is insane. Right?…Ahmadinejad was a vicious extremist when he was president of Iran. He was leading the chants of Death to America, absolutely vicious. So the idea that putting him in place as a moderate leader. That's bananas.”

Video

Question: Does Putin see US troop cuts as indicating it is less committed to NATO and Europe?

Polish MEP @michalkobosko : “I'm afraid he might read it this way, and that would be very bad for for for us Europeans, that would be very bad for the States because that might encourage Putin to start considering or reconsidering his paln… this is why we are asking our American partners to reconsider their thinking about the military presence in Europe.”

Video

New: The Internal Revenue Service can’t bring claims against President Donald Trump, his family or businesses for past tax issues, according to additional terms added Tuesday to the settlement the Justice Department reachedwith Trump to resolve his $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS.

For “The Return of Great Powers”, I asked former senior Trump advisors including John Bolton, John Kelly, Gen Mark Milley and others what they expected in a second Trump term. Together, they identified three risks:

- U.S. aid to Ukraine 
- U.S. support for NATO 
- U.S. aid to Taiwan 

They were right about all three.
